hint: Here the part is known and the whole is missing. If $20$ is only one tenth of the number, is the number bigger or smaller than $20$?

hints.text: Here the part is known and the whole is missing. If $20$ is only one tenth of the number, is the number bigger or smaller than $20$?
$10\%$ is one tenth, so the whole number is made of $10$ pieces that are each $20$. Work out $20 \times 10$.
Ten pieces of $20$ make $20 \times 10 = 200$, so the number is $200$.

explanation: $10\%$ means one tenth, so $20$ is one of ten equal pieces of the unknown number.
The whole is all ten pieces together, so multiply the piece by $10$: $20 \times 10 = 200$.
Check by going forward: $10\%$ of $200$ is $200 \div 10 = 20$, which is correct.
The number we were looking for is $200$.
